reviews.full_takes:
# Independent speech-to-text verification — arrival-v1

## Scope

The two successful, user-approved HeyGen takes were transcribed locally from their actual audio bytes. No new speech was generated, and no script text, initial prompt, hotwords, or provider timestamps were supplied to the recognition model. The script comparison took place only after inference.

Original filenames end in `.wav`, but the files contain MP3 audio. Their SHA-256 values are recorded in the JSON results.

## Method

- Implementation: faster-whisper 1.2.1 / CTranslate2, CPU int8, four threads.
- Full-take first pass: public `Systran/faster-whisper-base`, Spanish, beam size 5, temperature 0, previous-text conditioning disabled, VAD disabled.
- Targeted second pass: public `Systran/faster-whisper-small`, staff take only, with the same settings. This pass addressed concrete uncertainties in the base transcript, especially room 204.
- FFmpeg decoded the originals to 16 kHz mono float32 for model input. The original bytes remain unchanged. This input route avoided an installed faster-whisper 1.2.1 / PyAV 19 decoder API incompatibility.
- Word times are model estimates and must be cross-checked with actual waveform boundaries before cutting.
- Official implementation documentation: https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper

Comparison normalization ignores punctuation, capitalization, and written accents. It equates the numeric token `204` with `doscientos cuatro`, and `Wi-Fi` / `wi fi` with `wifi`. No other lexical differences are normalized away.

## Results

| Take / model | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Traveler / base | All eight lines match the approved wording after the stated normalization, including Alex Martín, the wifi question, and the repeat request. |
| Staff / base | Non-matching words: taxis → “táxices”, puede → “puedes”, tiene → “tienes”, and the room phrase → “lado 104”. These are ASR hypotheses, not confirmed synthesis defects. |
| Staff / small | Correctly recognizes taxis, singular puede, and room 204. The remaining difference is “¿Tienes su pasaporte?” versus “¿Tiene su pasaporte?”. |

The final staff small-model transcript is:

> Los taxis están afuera, a la derecha. Muy bien, puede salir por esa puerta. Buenas tardes. ¿A nombre de quién? Perfecto. ¿Tienes su pasaporte? Su habitación es la 204.

The traveler base-model transcript is:

> Hola, buenos días. ¿Dónde puedo tomar un taxi? Perfecto, gracias. Voy a este hotel. Gracias, muy amable. Buenas tardes. Tengo una reservación. A nombre de Alex Martín. Sí, aquí está. Gracias. ¿Cuál es la contraseña del Wi-Fi? ¿Me puede repetir por favor?

## Residual uncertainty

The approved sequence `tiene su` already contains an /s/ at the word boundary. ASR assigning that sound to `tienes` does not, by itself, prove that the synthesizer pronounced an extra /s/. Both model sizes produce the same boundary interpretation, so this result is retained as unresolved; it is not marked as an exact staff-script pass.

The waveform reviewer identified a signal burst at approximately 18.56–19.12 seconds in the staff source. Neither full-take ASR pass recognized a separate word there; both estimate the final “Su” around 19.7 seconds. Recognition output alone cannot classify that burst or justify cutting it away. Conservative boundaries and human listening remain necessary.

## Limits

### Subsequent final-excerpt check

The later check of all 14 finalized candidate clips is recorded in `final-clips/REVIEW.md`. Thirteen clips match the approved wording after normalization. The clipped hotel-05 question is recognized exactly as “¿Tiene su pasaporte?”, while airport-04 is recognized as “puedes salir” despite the full-take small-model result “puede salir”. The changing hypotheses reinforce the word-boundary uncertainty; no human listening or complete perceptual approval is implied. All expected opening and final words, including the room number 204, are recognized in the candidate clips.

This is machine transcription evidence only. The two model sizes belong to the same Whisper model family. They are independent of HeyGen's supplied text/timing metadata, not independent linguistic reviewers. ASR can normalize, omit, hallucinate, or misassign spoken words.

No human or perceptual listening approval was performed. These checks do not establish pleasant delivery, pronunciation quality, regional/Dominican accent, or the safety of every cut. The final excerpts require boundary verification, and the unresolved staff question requires explicit listening review before claiming complete script fidelity.

## Files

- `staff-asr.json`: full base staff transcript, estimated word timestamps, settings, source hash, and differences.
- `traveler-asr.json`: full base traveler transcript and word timestamps.
- `small/staff-asr.json`: targeted small-model staff transcript and timestamps.
- `summary.json` and `small/summary.json`: compact machine results.
- `../run_asr_verification.py`: reproducible validation script, with no reference transcript supplied to recognition.

# Final candidate excerpt ASR — arrival-v1

The 14 finalized MP3 candidate excerpts in `arrival-audio-work/clips/` were recognized once each, using cached local models. Staff clips used Whisper small; traveler clips used Whisper base. Inference used Spanish, CPU/int8, beam 5, temperature 0, no initial prompt, no hotwords, no expected script, and no provider word timestamps. Expected text was compared only afterward.

**Result: 13 of 14 excerpts exactly match the approved text after the documented punctuation/accent/number/Wi-Fi normalization.**

| Clip | Recognition result |
| --- | --- |
| airport-01 | Exact normalized match |
| airport-02 | Exact normalized match |
| airport-03 | Exact normalized match |
| airport-04 | Recognized “Muy bien, puedes salir por esa puerta.”; approved text is “Muy bien. Puede salir por esa puerta.” |
| airport-05 | Exact normalized match |
| hotel-01 | Exact normalized match |
| hotel-02 | Exact normalized match |
| hotel-03 | Exact normalized match, including initial “¿A” |
| hotel-04 | Exact normalized match, including initial “A” and Alex Martín |
| hotel-05 | Exact normalized match: “Perfecto. ¿Tiene su pasaporte?” |
| hotel-06 | Exact normalized match |
| hotel-07 | Exact normalized match, including initial “Su” and room 204 |
| hotel-08 | Exact normalized match |
| hotel-repeat | Exact normalized match, including initial “¿Me” |

No lost initial or final word was detected in this pass. This is a recognition-based boundary check, not proof that every phoneme or breath is preserved.

## Context-sensitive word-boundary hypotheses

The full staff take recognized with Whisper small gave the approved singular “puede salir”, while the final airport-04 excerpt gave “puedes salir”. Conversely, the full-take question gave “tienes su pasaporte”, while the final hotel-05 excerpt gave the approved “tiene su pasaporte”.

Both differences sit immediately before an s-initial next word. The hypotheses change with recognition context. They therefore do not, by themselves, establish an audible synthesis defect or a truncation caused by cutting. The differences are preserved in the reports; no transcript is silently rewritten to claim an exact match.

The extra staff-source signal burst at approximately18.56–19.12 seconds was retained inside hotel-07 by the waveform reviewer. ASR recognizes the intended room phrase and no additional word, but cannot classify that earlier burst or establish its perceptual acceptability.

## Limitations

No human or perceptual listening approval has been performed. ASR does not establish voice pleasantness, pronunciation quality, Dominican/regional accent, or suitability as a pronunciation model. The recordings remain technical candidates for listening review.

The source masters and excerpts were only read; this verification did not modify them or synthesize new audio.

## Evidence

`summary.json` retains every clip's SHA-256, expected and recognized wording, model, decoded duration, normalized match result, and comparison with full-take ASR. Individual `<clip-id>.json` files additionally contain estimated word timestamps.

`../../run_clip_asr_verification.py` reproduces this pass using the cached models.
